card werk-v0-conversations  [open]  PROPOSED — not in the map until it is accepted
In v0, a new conversation starts empty from a control in the tab strip, with the open card as its home card
why: The chat card says a person can keep more than one conversation, but the cards that define forking, parking and the tab strip are not decided. v0 needs one plain way to start a second conversation, so it starts an empty one and leaves the rest for later.

A person can keep more than one conversation (see #werk-chat). To make that possible without the undecided tab features, v0 gives the tab strip one control that starts a new conversation. The new conversation gets its own agent process (see #werk-chat-stdin) and an empty session. Its home card is the card open when it starts, and the home card is its tab label (see #werk-mc-split).

Each tab is a chip in the tab strip. A click on a chip switches the chat pane to that conversation and shows its newest message (see #werk-mc-tab-bottom). A tab whose agent died, or that has a running background agent, shows it as #werk-mc-live-dead and #werk-mc-bgagents say. Every conversation stays on the strip; v0 has no close, no park and no idle sweep.

Forking a session, reading a sibling conversation, parking a tab and keyboard shortcuts for tabs are not in v0.

Example:

- The map shows card A "We charge per seat". Conversation C1 has A as its home card.

1. The person opens card B "The invoice shows the seat count" and presses the new-conversation control.
2. A new tab C2 appears with the label B. Its agent starts with an empty session.
3. The person sends a message in C2. The turn names B as the open card.
4. The person clicks C1. The pane shows the newest message of C1.

```
tab strip:  [ A ]  [ B ]  [ + ]
             C1     C2     new conversation, empty, home card = open card
```

why: Several conversations in tabs are postponed, but some decided chat rules are written for tabs. Reading each tab rule as a rule for the one conversation keeps those rules in v0 without the tab strip.

v0 builds one continuous conversation per project in the chat pane (see #werk-onechat), with no tab strip, no fork and no park (see #werk-multichat, which is postponed).

A rule that names a tab applies to that one conversation. The background line shows in its pane (see #werk-mc-bgagents). The dead mark stays until the next child starts (see #werk-mc-live-dead). A dead child has no other pane in the same project to show a line in, so its error shows in its own pane, and the project switcher marks the project as dead beside the busy mark (see #werk-projects-switcher).

Example:

1. The child of C exits with an error that a retry cannot fix.
2. The switcher row of P shows the dead mark.
3. The person opens P. The pane of C shows the error at the end of the turn.
4. The person sends a message in C. A new child starts, and the dead mark goes.

A fork carries the parent's whole history (see #werk-mc-fork). That is wrong for an unrelated topic. To give that topic a clean start without a second button, '+' (see #werk-mc-open) has a long press: a press held for about half a second. The long press opens a small menu above '+' with two rows, each with an icon before its label: "Fork current conversation" and "New empty conversation". The fork row is in bold, because a short press on '+' does the same thing. A right-click on '+' opens the same menu. A short press on '+' forks at once, with no menu. "New empty conversation" opens a new tab at the open card, with no parent session. The first message in that tab starts a session with no history. The only other empty start is a fork of a tab that has no session yet (see #werk-mc-fork-nosession).

"New empty conversation" never switches to an existing tab. A fork switches to a tab that already has the card as its home. "New empty conversation" opens a new tab every time, also on that card. The new tab still takes the open card as its home and its chip label (see #werk-mc-split).

Example:

- tab "main", home card "#map", active. The map shows "#fold".
- tab "fold", home card "#fold".

1. The person Shift+clicks a link to "#fold". The pane switches to tab "fold". No tab opens.
2. The person goes back to "main". The map shows "#fold" again.
3. The person holds '+' down. The menu opens. No tab opens yet.
4. The person clicks outside the menu. The menu closes. Nothing else happens.
5. The person holds '+' again and picks "New empty conversation". A second "#fold" chip opens and becomes active. Its conversation has no history.

```
start:              [#map*] [#fold]           +
Shift+click #fold:  [#map]  [#fold*]          +   (switch, no new tab)
new empty on #fold: [#map]  [#fold] [#fold*]  +   (new tab, no history)

*  the active tab
+  a short press forks, a long press opens the menu
```

Extending #werk-mc-split-plus does not work, because the long press already has a card. #werk-mc-empty-control (decided, postponed with multichat) defines it.

Its rules conflict with #werk-mc-split-plus:
- **Short press:** #werk-mc-empty-control makes it fork the current conversation. #werk-mc-split-plus makes it start an empty conversation.
- **Long press:** #werk-mc-empty-control opens a menu with "Fork current conversation" and "New empty conversation". If forking is postponed, that menu has one row, so there is nothing to long-press for.

So the two cards describe two stages of the same button. #werk-mc-split-plus is the stage before forking exists. #werk-mc-empty-control is the stage after.

Options:
1. **Rewrite #werk-mc-split-plus as the full `+` behaviour, with fork and long press.** The long press moves in from #werk-mc-empty-control, which I would then drop. This keeps one card per control. The cost is that it depends on the postponed #werk-mc-fork, so it is postponed too.
2. **Keep both and fix the contradiction.** #werk-mc-split-plus says the short press starts empty only until forking exists. #werk-mc-empty-control stays the owner of the long press. This keeps the postponed fork cards out of the live card.
3. **Discard #werk-mc-tabs-new-button only.** It is a ghost that duplicates #werk-mc-split-plus with less detail. This is needed with either option above.

I recommend option 2, plus option 3. The long press stays on a card that is already decided, and no card has to take on a dependency on a postponed one.

card werk-mc-split  [decided]
A conversation has a home card, not a subtree boundary
why: Focus is a label, not a fence. A conversation crosses subtrees whether you allow it or not.
subtree: 2 cards, 1 open, 1 decided

The two obvious options are 'arbitrary split' and 'per-subtree focus'. Neither fits. The third:

A conversation records the card that was open when it started. That id is its name, its tab label, and the seed context sent on its first turn. It is not a fence. The conversation may navigate anywhere, and the pane keeps sending the open card on every turn.

Why not a real subtree fence: a conversation that opens at #root can end up writing under #werk-chat. A fence would block it or force a switch. The map's tree is where a card sits; it is not where a thought stays.

What the home card buys, with no fence:

card werk-mc-split-plus  [open]
A short press on the plus button forks the conversation, and a long press offers an empty one
why: A person needs one control for both starts of a second conversation. A fork carries the parent's history, which is wrong for an unrelated topic, so a long press on the same button offers a clean start without a second button. Both starts take the open card as the new tab's home card, so the button needs no other input.

The tab strip ends with a + button. A short press forks the conversation on the open card (see #werk-mc-fork): the new tab keeps the parent's history, takes the open card as its home card and chip label (see #werk-mc-split), and takes the focus. A fork switches to a tab that already has the card as its home.

A long press, a press held for about half a second, or a right-click opens a small menu above +. It has two rows, each with an icon before its label: "Fork current conversation", in bold because a short press does the same, and "New empty conversation". A fork brings the parent's history, which is wrong for an unrelated topic, so the second row gives a clean start without a second button. "New empty conversation" opens a new tab every time, also on a card that already has a tab, because a switch to an existing tab would show an old conversation. The new tab has no parent session and starts no agent until its first message. That agent starts with an empty session. A click outside the menu closes it and nothing else happens.

Example:

- tab "main", home card "#map", active. The map shows "#fold".
- tab "fold", home card "#fold".

1. The person Shift+clicks a link to "#fold". The pane switches to tab "fold". No tab opens.
2. The person goes back to "main". The map shows "#fold" again.
3. The person presses + briefly. "main" forks: a new "#fold" tab opens with the history of "main".
4. The person holds + down. The menu opens. No tab opens yet.
5. The person picks "New empty conversation". Another "#fold" chip opens and takes the focus. Its conversation has no history.

short +:    [#map]  [#fold] [#fold*]         +   (fork, history kept)
empty:      [#map]  [#fold] [#fold] [#fold*] +   (new tab, no history)

*  the active tab
+  a short press forks, a long press opens the menu
```
